content.comment_body: Does anyone have experience with what happens if [product_name]'s input receives L+ or L1 voltage, but the device itself isn't powered at its own power input? This could occur if [product_name] is connected to an external device with its own power source and [product_name]'s power is interrupted (for example, due to a blown fuse). Could this situation damage [product_name]? Appreciate any advice.

analysis.insight_summary: Users are concerned about the reliability and protection of [product_name] when voltage is present at the input terminals but the device itself is unpowered. The main UX challenge is uncertainty regarding possible hardware damage in these scenarios due to a lack of clear specifications, which affects user trust in installation and troubleshooting processes.
analysis.user_expectations: Users want clear information on whether it is safe for [product_name]'s inputs to be energized while the unit itself isn't powered, including if there is any risk of damage or if protection mechanisms are present to handle these situations.
